steps: Review task, asset, finding and resource cards
Open a card to inspect its underlying records
Compare status charts with current resource use
dashboard.check: Statistics summarize stored records. If counts seem stale, refresh and inspect the detail list before changing concurrency.

steps: Check collection capability and last activity first
Filter by type, severity and source IP
Open evidence and inspect target, time, count and confidence
Review the exact scope before changing bans or allowlists
attackAlert.check: Historical alerts may remain available when automatic collection is unsupported. Check deployment and collector status separately from record counts.

steps: Filter installed and store tools by category and source
Click a card to read its standard documentation
Upload a supported file or ZIP and review entry, parameters and dependencies
Enable only the tools needed by the workflow
systemExtension.check: Availability, enabled state and execution are distinct. Long documentation opens in a drawer. Inspect package structure and dependency errors after a failed upload.

steps: Enter a reachable IP or domain. Windows adds the receiver port automatically; explicit ports are accepted. Incomplete fields show a prompt. Node mode requires an endpoint, fingerprint and credential. Choose limited validity and categories before generating a link; no migration starts yet.
Paste the full invitation and approve pairing within30 seconds; request a concrete sync plan and await peer approval, with automatic timeout rejection.

Click a record summary for its progress, stage, categories and results. Completed, failed, rejected or expired records can be removed; active or pending operations cannot. Imported business data and protocol retry receipts remain.
controlSync.check: Verify the saved state and results shown on the page.

steps: Create a group, share its invitation and approve participants
Enter the independent workspace and choose group or direct conversation
Manage members, names and cohost service separately from applications
Stage files below the composer, remove unwanted files and send

Choose findings, reports or full sessions from the detailed list. Findings include AI, PoC and kernel scan sources. Both sides click the sent card to preview; recipients save it into the corresponding system list. Repeated saves are idempotent. Sessions remain paused with no AI call. Ordinary attachments use file download.
Add a workspace node, verify its fingerprint, then select a delivery policy
collaboration.check: Direct content is limited to the two participants. Viewing the latest message marks that conversation read. Cohost service requires consent and prepared public data; it does not grant administrative approval rights.

steps: Filter tasks and open their details
Inspect sites, ports, domains and findings separately
Confirm stop, resume or restart against the actual status
Review asset and linked-session options before deleting
tasks.check: Submission is not completion. Diagnose failures from task details and logs; avoid repeatedly creating the same task.

steps: Name the task and choose a policy
Select the target type and enter the corresponding scope
Review exclusions, groups, scan options and resource hints
Submit and track the created task
taskCreate.check: Group links can prefill scope. Automatic AI requires a configured model; use Go to configuration to complete missing settings before submitting.

steps: Create or edit a reusable policy
Choose the required discovery and detection stages
Configure optional automatic AI behavior
Save, reopen and select the policy from a task or schedule
policy.check: Check dependent schedules before deletion. Resolve validation messages and missing model configuration before saving.

steps: Enter name, policy, time and preferred model on the first step
Optionally select backup and supervisory models
Continue to the editable target and optional asset group
Submit and inspect the next execution and created task
taskSchedule.check: An empty backup is valid. Group selection assists target entry. Disabling a schedule stops future triggers, not tasks already created.

steps: Filter system, manual or workgroup session origins
Open a session and inspect scope, events, findings and reports
Continue, pause or finish according to status and permission
Review the deletion scope before confirming
pentest.check: Origin describes creation; status describes execution. Waiting for a model or human input is not itself a failure.

steps: Create a manual session or resume an existing one
Choose model, execution mode and scope, then send instructions
Inspect tool results, files and approvals and pause when needed
Open the browser or Burps and review traffic before replay
Upload supporting files and organize evidence at the end
pentestConsole.check: Human mode waits for input. TCP/TLS replay requires an explicit port; use hex or Base64 for binary data and session-specific CA or client certificates for TLS.

steps: Close WeChat and clear the displayed package directory
Reopen and load the intended mini program, then upload its new wx folder
Review extracted endpoints and information
Choose intensity, autonomous or human mode and preferred or optional backup AI
Inspect HTTP/HTTPS evidence in the resulting session
miniapp.check: Avoid mixing old packages. Extracted clues are not confirmed findings; check package completeness after parsing errors. Human mode creates a waiting session.

steps: Pair the device using the supported wired or wireless flow
For wireless, configure parameters and search
Choose traffic egress in the app and configure HTTPS trust as needed
Generate authorized test traffic and inspect HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket or raw TCP
Send a record to Burps with the matching protocol and encoding
appPentest.check: TLS plaintext requires appropriate interception and trust conditions. Pairing alone does not prove traffic capture. Diagnose device connectivity before relay status.

steps: Inspect probe status and last contact
Create or pair a probe and verify connection parameters
Select an available probe for the task and inspect returned evidence
Check dependent work before removal
probeManage.check: A saved probe record does not prove a running process. For offline probes, check reachability, credentials and probe logs.

steps: Collapsed by default: calls, total tokens, input/output and failed calls stay visible. Expand for model and stage breakdowns. Refresh reads statistics without calling a model; global parameters keep their layout.

Add a binding, choose a uniquely named configured model and required built-in stages, upload the bundle and select its entry. Both model name and stage must match. Guard bindings require risk confirmation. Legacy unscoped bindings need stages; built-in tool and safety constraints remain.
aiConfig.check: Verify the saved state and results shown on the page.

steps: Choose AI, kernel scan or workgroup source
Filter and open an individual finding
Read evidence and impact before editing or changing verification state
Review single or batch scope for reports, sharing and deletion
vulnCenter.check: Live updates retain the active filter. Unrated means available evidence cannot establish severity; it is not an informational rating.

steps: Create a report template, upload Word, then choose manual marking or AI learning. Manual marking edits the original document with natural language and tags; learning can call a model. Both require review. Existing text templates remain editable.
reportEdit.check: Verify the saved state and results shown on the page.

steps: Search and inspect an existing rule and prerequisites
Create or import supported metadata and validation content
Save and select it in an authorized workflow
Review policy dependencies before editing or removing
poc.check: A rule is not evidence that every target is vulnerable. Diagnose format errors and check product version, path, port and network results.

steps: Search product or vulnerability identifiers and filter severity
Read affected versions, scores and source references
Inspect the locally exploitable field and available material
Match the entry to actual asset versions before validation
vulnIntel.check: Unrated is incomplete source data. Locally exploitable describes available material, not guaranteed exploitation on every target.

steps: Locate records by session, target and organization. Targets branch to independent findings; explicit parent steps or findings create continuations. Intranet entry points are labelled separately.

Enter a source session ID, target text, organization or state and search. Reset clears filters. Target text is treated literally, not as a regular expression; source columns and node details support traceability.

Open a graph preview to pan, zoom and inspect targets, sessions and references in a movable dialog. Independent findings branch from targets; chronology alone does not imply causation. The console reuses this same graph component.
attackChain.check: Verify the saved state and results shown on the page.

steps: Choose an intelligence type and query its sources
Open records and compare dates and references
Import or maintain supported entries
Relate useful information to local assets
intel.check: Source and date affect reliability. Retain references and compare identifiers before merging apparent duplicates.

steps: Select an asset type and query stored records
Inspect matching fields, timestamps and ownership
Open site, port, domain or certificate details
Organize useful scope into an asset group
search.check: Searching stored assets does not start a network scan. Broaden filters and verify the asset type when no result appears.

steps: Create a named scope with explicit exclusions
Open the group and inspect assets
Use its task entry and review the prefilled scope and policy
Check schedules before modifying or deleting
assetGroups.check: A group organizes scope, not scan completion. Exclusions matter; if group scope changes, refresh and confirm again before submission.

steps: Create monitoring scope, policy and interval
Check enabled state and previous or next run
Inspect added, removed or changed assets
Review future triggers before pausing or deleting
assetMonitor.check: Comparison requires samples. No changes does not mean no execution; inspect the last run and errors.

steps: Search recognition rules and inspect matching conditions
Create or edit product metadata and supported patterns
Save and check controlled samples for false positives
Review identified technology in later task results
fingerprint.check: Fingerprints identify clues, not vulnerabilities. Broad patterns can misidentify products; rule changes affect subsequent detection.

steps: Enter search terms, scope and required API configuration
Submit and monitor status
Open repository, file, location and context for each match
Preserve required evidence before deleting
githubTasks.check: A match may be an example or stale material. Check API limits and reachability after failures; redact sensitive content in evidence.

steps: Create query scope and an interval
Enable and inspect the last run
Compare new matches with prior content
Check the next run after changing or disabling
githubMonitor.check: Recurring monitoring differs from one-off search. Review execution errors before interpreting empty results; account for provider limits.

steps: Identify the account and inspect roles
Create a user with the required minimum permissions
Review dependencies before changing password, disabling or deleting
Verify menus and actions with the resulting permissions
userManage.check: API permissions remain enforced in addition to menu visibility. Keep an administrator available and manage running work through its business workflow.

steps: Select a proxy group and supported protocol
Enter host, port, authentication and intended use
Save and run the connection test
Select the proxy in the relevant workflow and verify actual egress
proxy.check: A single successful probe does not guarantee every target. Unsaved drafts differ from active settings; never expose authentication in troubleshooting output.

steps: Choose the capability or destination to test
Run diagnostics and wait for individual results
Distinguish DNS, connection, TLS and latency failures
Correct the relevant settings and compare a new result
networkCheck.check: Tests run from the platform location, which differs from phones and remote probes. Inspect the failing stage before changing global settings.

steps: Configure and save each required provider
Test access and check permission or quota
Set notification thresholds and inspect the read-only platform ID
Configure destinations and send a test
apiKeys.check: Platform ID is the activation JWT uid. Notifications include system and ID to identify origin; verify the receiver actually obtained the test.

steps: Choose log type or task and filter level or keyword
Read surrounding events in time order
Refresh or download supported logs
Repeat the query after applying a fix
logs.check: Early Windows startup can fail before service.log exists. Use the startup.log path shown by the startup diagnostic screen.

steps: Filter requests by time, path or source
Inspect method, status, latency and identity clues
Correlate application logs at the same time
Export only the required permitted scope
accessLog.check: HTTP status is not the entire business result. Platform access logs differ from captured traffic to a target.

steps: Filter traffic by action, status, target or time
Inspect request, response and decision reason
Open the related session to see whether an action was approved and sent
Keep redacted evidence for review
guardLog.check: Raw TCP and missing responses do not invent HTTP status codes. Distinguish supervisory denial from a target response.

steps: Expand a parent and choose a menu leaf
Search a feature name or text and expand its matching group
Read purpose, features, steps and result guidance
Open the associated page or reload the chapter URL
manual.check: This manual works offline. Permissions, current state and configuration still govern available actions; clear the search to restore the full directory.

steps: Review activation status and credential expiry
Use the supported activation flow to add a credential
Check the read-only platform ID below the credential list
Refresh status after renewal
activation.check: Platform ID is the JWT uid, not an editable nickname. Keep credentials private and check product type, expiry and system time after errors.

steps: Read current version and available update status
Review compatibility and active work
Start the update and wait through check, download, validation and restart
Verify version, accounts, settings and data
updateCheck.check: A test iteration is not formal publication. Never bypass signature errors; use the update recovery flow after interruption and the version distribution contract for patch rules.

steps: History is read from files delivered with the installed version, without fetching remote history. System updates open by default; switch to patch updates for fixes to existing features.

Feature additions/removals belong to system versions; existing-feature fixes belong to patches. Patch serials stay hidden in the main version label. Test iterations are development builds, not formal releases.
changelog.check: Verify the saved state and results shown on the page.

steps: Read project information and supplied links
Prepare version, reproduction steps and redacted logs before feedback
developer.check: External links require connectivity. Include the actual error and stage, but exclude tokens, credentials and private data.
